fix(hosted): no popups or top navigation, give feedback instead (#695)

A host that embeds the hosted bundle in an iframe sandboxed without
allow-popups and allow-top-navigation got silent no-ops: opening a PDF
attachment (window.open on a blob URL) and the help and website links
did nothing.

- One helper, js/core/extern-openen.js, is now the only place that opens
  anything outside the app: openExtern(url) for links, biedBijlageAan()
  for attachments and biedDownloadAan() for an <a download>.
- Desktop (Tauri) keeps the shell plugin path, the plain web build keeps
  opening a new tab.
- Hosted: a link shows its address in a Windows-style message with a
  read-only, selectable field; an attachment becomes a download with a
  short message. The build-time mode check lets Rollup drop the
  window.open branches, so the hosted bundle contains none.
- Release-notes links (target=_blank) are intercepted when hosted.
- The unused stock PDF.js viewer from public/ (viewer.html with its own
  window.open) is left out of the hosted bundle; cmaps, standard fonts
  and wasm stay.
- New texts in all 40 locales.

Tests: extern-openen.test.mjs (behaviour per environment plus a source
guard: no window.open outside the helper, no location assignments, no
target=_blank without a hosted click handler) and
scripts/verify-gast-popups.mjs (npm run verify:hosted-popups), which
searches the built hosted bundle and drives it in headless Chromium in a
sandboxed cross-origin iframe.

feat(hosted): set up the host storage contract from the iframe (#694)

The hosted build now sets up window.__OPDS_HOST__ itself when it runs in
an iframe opened with #ouder=<origin>&app=pdf&bestand=<id>, so a host no
longer has to inject a script into index.html. An existing __OPDS_HOST__
still wins.

- js/core/host-brug.js: the postMessage bridge as pure logic. ouder must
  be exactly scheme://host[:port]; location.ancestorOrigins[0] must match
  where the browser knows it; only messages with event.source ===
  window.parent and event.origin === ouder count, and messages go only to
  ouder. Requests { werkplek: 1, id, soort, ... }, replies { werkplek: 1,
  antwoord, ok, waarde | fout }. Handshake "hallo" every 250 ms, giving
  up after 60 s; 120 s per request. open fetches adres with credentials
  omit, no-store and redirect error; opslaan transfers its own copy of
  the bytes as an ArrayBuffer; lijst and versies map onto the contract.
- js/core/host-brug-start.js: wires it up at startup of the hosted build
  only; the desktop build drops the branch at build time.
- A failed open shows "The file could not be read from storage. Try
  again."; a host that never answers shows a clear message. Both are
  translated into all 40 locales.
- Unit tests with a fake clock and fake windows cover parsing and
  validating ouder, ignoring other origins and windows, the handshake,
  the timeouts and request/response matching.
- scripts/gehost-brug-e2e.mjs (npm run test:hosted-bridge, also a Linux
  CI step): the unchanged hosted bundle on one origin in a sandboxed
  iframe of a test page on another origin, in headless Chromium. It
  opens the document from bestand, saves a rectangle back (checked in
  the bytes the host received), lists the versions, and ignores forged
  replies from a third origin and from another window on the right
  origin.

feat(release): attach the hosted web bundle to every release (#692)

The release workflow gets a web-bundle job that runs after the version
check in create-release. It builds the hosted bundle once per tag with a
relative base (--base=./), so the same files work under any sub-path, and
attaches open-pdf-studio-web-<version>.tar.gz with a .sha256 next to it.

The archive holds the dist plus:
- MANIFEST.sha256: the SHA-256 of every file (sha256sum -c format)
- THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt: licence, author and the full licence and notice
  files of every npm package rollup put into the bundle, plus the licence
  files that already ship as separate files
- bron.json: version, tag, commit, licence and source link; the packer
  refuses to run when the tag is known and points to another commit

npm run pack:hosted builds and packs (own deterministic ustar writer, no
new dependency). npm run verify:hosted-bundle checks the archive hash and
the manifest, unpacks the bundle under /pdf/ and /tools/pdf/ of a static
server and opens a PDF with standard fonts and a CJK CMap in headless
Chromium, failing on any request outside the bundle folder. The job runs
the same check before uploading.

feat(hosted): make the hosted index.html CSP-ready with SRI, without inline code (#693)

A small vite plugin (scripts/gehost-html.mjs) post-processes index.html in
hosted mode only, on the files as written to disk:
- inline <style> moves into opds-vooraf.css; an inline <script> or a
  reference to another host fails the build
- every <script src>, <link rel=stylesheet> and <link rel=modulepreload>
  gets integrity="sha384-..." and crossorigin="anonymous"

The desktop build is byte-for-byte unchanged and tauri.conf.json is not
touched. No new dependency.

npm run test:hosted-csp builds the hosted bundle (or takes --dist), serves
it under /pdf/ with exactly the policy from the issue as the only extra
header, and in headless Chromium opens a PDF, renders it, draws a rectangle
and saves; it requires zero securitypolicyviolation events, zero console
errors and a Square annotation in the saved file. A control page on the
same server proves the detector sees an inline script, an eval in the page
and an eval in a worker. The test runs as a CI job in ci.yml and against
the released files in the web-bundle release job; verify:hosted-bundle
also checks index.html.

Merge branch 'fix/695-hosted-no-popups' into integratie/supercloud-2026.43

fix(hosted): keep the desktop-only tab drag plugin out of the web bundle

The tab drag plugin was pulled into the hosted bundle through a dynamic
import, although dragging a tab out of the window only works on the
desktop. It has no licence metadata, so it appeared as UNKNOWN in the
third-party notices of the release archive. The import now drops out
of the hosted build; a source test guards it.

ci(hosted): run the browser jobs on ubuntu-24.04

ubuntu-latest moved to 26.04, where Playwright 1.59 cannot install
Chromium, so the hosted-csp job failed before running any test. Pin the
hosted-csp job and the release web-bundle job to ubuntu-24.04.
